findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update can miss changes because it uses an organization-aware model
findings.body: update() retrieves the current identity provider via getById(), which returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() also checks whether the linked organization exists and is enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), whose ENABLED filter calls this overridden isEnabled(). If the linked organization is disabled or missing, the original model is treated as not available for login even though it may still be present in the .idp.login cache. An update that changes hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or BROKER_PUBLIC while the organization is disabled can therefore hit the 'both not login' no-invalidation branch, leaving stale cached login lists. When the organization is enabled again, getForLogin() can return identity providers that should now be hidden, link-only, or not public. The invalidation decision should be based on the raw persisted IDP fields (or the delegate model), not the organization-aware dynamic isEnabled(), and/or organization lifecycle changes should invalidate these login caches.

findings.title: REALM_ONLY login cache entries are duplicated per organizationId
findings.body: getForLogin() uses organizationId as the search key for all fetch modes. For FetchMode.REALM_ONLY the organizationId parameter is semantically ignored, so calls with different organization IDs can create separate cached search entries under the same REALM_ONLY cache key containing the same realm-level identity providers. This wastes cache space and can cause unnecessary delegate lookups. For REALM_ONLY, organizationId should be normalized to the empty search key.

findings.title: Single login cache entry accumulates results for all organization IDs
findings.body: The login cache is keyed only by realm and FetchMode, while different organizationId values are stored as additional search keys inside the same IdentityProviderListQuery. In realms with many organizations, the ORG_ONLY/ALL cache entry can grow without bound as distinct organization logins occur, and any qualifying identity-provider change invalidates the whole entry. This can create a large cache object and a contention hotspot. Consider per-organization cache keys or another strategy to bound the accumulated search-key state.

findings.title: Cleanup removes literal "alias" instead of the created identity provider aliases
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registration uses testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove instead of the actual created alias ("idp-alias-" + i). The same mistake occurs later for idp-alias-20. As a result, the test does not clean up the identity providers it creates and may attempt to remove a nonexistent provider named "alias", leaking realm state or causing cleanup failures.
